story.title: Ebola Outbreak in DR Congo Exceeds 1,000 Deaths
story.summary: The ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has resulted in over 1,000 confirmed deaths, according to official government data. The World Health Organization has indicated that the actual number of cases may be significantly higher, potentially two to four times the reported figures.

explore_lenses.label: Who is most affected, and why is containment hard?
explore_lenses.title: Eastern DRC communities face layered risks
explore_lenses.summary: The outbreak is centered in Ituri Province, where displacement, insecurity, limited health infrastructure and population movement make finding cases and interrupting transmission more difficult.

claims.text: WHO says the outbreak is occurring in a remote, densely populated area affected by a humanitarian crisis, insecurity, and substantial population and trade movements.
WHO reported 1,926 confirmed cases and 702 cumulative deaths as of 11 July, citing the DRC National Institute of Public Health; affected communities include internally displaced people near Bunia.

DRC health authorities and response partners have made community dialogue central to the response, while WHO identifies community engagement, surveillance, contact tracing and cross-border preparedness as core control measures.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: Published counts are likely incomplete because access, surveillance and reporting are constrained in conflict-affected and mobile populations.

explore_lenses.label: Why is this Ebola outbreak unusually difficult to treat?
explore_lenses.title: The virus type lacks approved countermeasures
explore_lenses.summary: This is Bundibugyo virus disease, an Ebola disease for which no vaccine or treatment has been approved, unlike some outbreaks caused by Ebola-Zaire virus.

claims.text: Laboratory analysis confirmed Bundibugyo virus, and CDC says it is likely spread by direct contact with an infected person's body fluids; people are most infectious late in illness and after death.

WHO and CDC state that there were no approved Bundibugyo-virus-specific vaccines or therapeutics at the time of their updates; care therefore includes supportive measures such as fluids, electrolyte replacement, oxygen, blood-pressure management and pain control.

WHO, INRB, the University of Oxford and partners began enrolling patients in the PARTNERS randomized trial to test MBP134, remdesivir and their combination; these are investigational treatments, not established effective therapies.

explore_lenses.label: How certain are the reported toll and outlook?
explore_lenses.title: Official totals are a floor, not a final measure
explore_lenses.summary: The death toll confirms an exceptionally severe emergency, but it should not be read as a complete count of infections or deaths; WHO and CDC both describe substantial under-detection uncertainty.

claims.text: Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya said 1,031 deaths had been confirmed, while the DRC Health Ministry had recorded 2,473 cases as of 20 July; WHO cautioned that the true outbreak size could be two to four times the official figures.

WHO documented significant uncertainty about the number of infections, geographic spread and epidemiological links, citing clusters of compatible community deaths, limited detection, and early high test positivity.

Forecast: In CDC scenarios published in June, if control measures remained weak, the model estimated a 65% chance of exceeding 20,000 cases within three months; with 70% of patients isolated, it estimated a 1-in-20 chance of reaching 10,000 cases. These were conditional projections, not predictions of what will occur.

related_stories.title: Wildfire Forces Evacuation of Nearly 12,000 Tourists in Southwest France
related_stories.summary: A wildfire in Le Porge, southwest France, has led to the evacuation of nearly 12,000 people, primarily tourists. The fire, which began around midday on Wednesday, has prompted a significant response from hundreds of firefighters battling the flames. The region has been experiencing extreme heat, contributing to the wildfire's rapid spread.

related_stories.title: France Evacuates 20,000 Amid Wildfires in Southwestern Region
related_stories.summary: Approximately 20,000 people have been evacuated from towns and holiday resorts in southwestern France due to a raging wildfire near the coastal town of Lege Cap-Ferret. Most of those evacuated were tourists from campsites around Arcachon Bay in the Gironde region.

related_stories.title: FDA Advisory Committee Reviews Peptide Accessibility and Safety
related_stories.summary: An FDA advisory committee is convening to evaluate the accessibility and safety of over six peptides that have gained popularity as wellness treatments. Critics highlight the lack of sufficient data on their efficacy and safety, raising concerns about their promotion by influencers. The discussions aim to determine whether to ease restrictions on these substances.

related_stories.title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Tankers Raise Oil Price Concerns
related_stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels, backed by Iran, have attacked two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, raising concerns about the future of oil and gas prices. This incident may represent a new front in the ongoing conflict involving the US and Iran, prompting discussions on its potential economic impact, particularly on gas prices in the United States.
